EXECUTIVE ORDER 10444
Amendment  op E xecutive  O rder N o.
88091  op J une  28, 1941, Establishing
the G ood C onduct  M edal, as
Amended by  E xecutive  O rder N o.
93233  of M arch 31, 1943
Executive Order No. 8809 of June 28, 
1941, establishing the Good Conduct 
Medal, as amended by Executive Order 
No. 9323 of March 31, 1943, is hereby 
further amended to read as follows:
“By virtue of the authority vested in 
me as President of the United States and 
as Commander in Chief of the Armed 
Forces of the United States, it is ordered 
as follows:
“There is hereby established the Good 
Conduct Medal, which shall include 
suitable appurtenances. Such medal 
may be ^warded for exemplary behavior, 
efficiency, and fidelity, under such regu­
lations as the Secretary of the Army and 
the Secretary of the Air Force shall 
severally prescribe, to those enlisted 
men of the Army of the United States 
and the'United States Air Force who on 
or after August 27, 1940, had or shall 
have honorably completed three years of 
active Federal military service, or who 
after December 7, 1941, have or shall- 
have honorably served one year of active 
Federal military service while the 
United States is at war, or who at the 
time of the termination of their active 
Federal military service have not previ­
ously been awarded a Good Conduct 
Medal and have completed a period of 
honorable service of less than three 
years if any part of that period of service 
has been performed after June 27, 1950: 
Provided,  that no persons, except per­
sons ¡separated from the active Federal 
military service by reason of physical 
disability incurred in line of duty, shall, 
be awarded such medal for a period of 
service of less than one year.”

versions.research_rationale:
Read the whole order (18 FR 2069, signed 1953-04-10; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10444.txt): it further amends Executive Order 8809 of June 28, 1941 (Good Conduct Medal), as amended by Executive Order 9323 of March 31, 1943, to read as a single restated paragraph, issued under the President's authority as President and Commander in Chief (no authority statute is cited). The restated text establishes the Good Conduct Medal for exemplary behavior, efficiency and fidelity under regulations the Secretary of the Army and the Secretary of the Air Force prescribe, for enlisted men of the Army and Air Force who on or after August 27, 1940 completed three years of active Federal military service, or served one year after December 7, 1941 while the United States is at war, or at the end of service had completed less than three years if any part was after June 27, 1950, with a proviso that no one except persons separated for physical disability incurred in line of duty receives it for under one year. The order has no own-terms end. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes. later-events:ofr_catalog has 1 hit, the Office of the Federal Register note that this order amends EO 8809 (with a see-reference to EO 9323); that is the order's own effect on its parent, not a later event against it. current-law:usc has 1 hit: 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, pt. II, ch. 57 note, which prints Ex. Ord. No. 8809 as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 9323, Ex. Ord. No. 10444 (Apr. 10, 1953, 18 F.R. 2069) and Ex. Ord. No. 14085 (section 2, Oct. 3, 2022, 87 F.R. 60541) with no ending statement (release point 119-121, through 2026-10-09). current-law:ecfr has 1 hit that is only a search lead and states no ending. The held text of Executive Order 14085 (87 FR 60541) section 2 amends Executive Order 8809 as amended by 9323 and 10444 by striking men and inserting members and by adding references to the Space Force on or after December 20, 2019 after the August 27, 1940, December 7, 1941 and June 27, 1950 dates; it is recorded as a later event, and under the strike-and-insert ruling the clause continues, amended. The Federal Register issue of April 14, 1953 also prints Army and Air Force regulation notes (32 CFR 578.27 and 878.46, indexed by the packet as an EO 10445 item) whose editorial notes only refer to this order; they are not amendments or an end. The held-corpus search for the number 10444 found no revocation or supersession.

The only later instrument found, Executive Order 14085 section 2 (effective 2022-10-03), amends it and keeps it in force; the U.S. Code note still prints it without an ending statement, and the held-corpus search for the number 10444 found no revocation or supersession.","independent_command_check":"The restatement of the parent order is completed by the text it sets out; there is no separate one-time command, deadline or revocation, and nothing in the clause is exhausted by performance. The restated eligibility rule is a standing rule that continues with the medal.","savings_check":"No saving clause or transitional provision appears in the order. Eligibility dates in the restated paragraph (August 27, 1940; December 7, 1941; June 27, 1950) are standing eligibility criteria, not time limits on the clause. The bounded searches found no preserved right or pending matter needing separate treatment.","scope_check":"One clause covers the whole text (characters 624-2365): the amending instruction and the restated paragraph establishing the Good Conduct Medal, its eligibility rules and its proviso. The order has no numbered sections, so the inventory is a single clause. Executive Order 14085 section 2 changes wording inside the restated paragraph (men to members; Space Force date insertions) within the same clause."}
